subject: Strength of Materials
summary: Euler buckling and effective lengths, slenderness ratio, Rankine's formula, strain energy (axial, bending, torsion, impact), Castigliano's theorem, and strain gauges and rosettes

questions.text: The steel column shown is a tube of 50 mm outer and 40 mm inner diameter, 2.5 m long, with both ends pinned. For E = 200 GPa, its Euler buckling load is nearly
solution: Concept: Euler load Pcr = π²EI/Le², with Le = L for both ends pinned.
Exam tip: 228.8 kN treats the ends as fixed (Le = L/2) and 14.3 kN as fixed at one end with the other end free (Le = 2L). Read the end conditions first.

questions.text: The aluminium strut shown (40 mm × 25 mm rectangular section, 0.8 m long) is fixed at its base and its top end is not restrained. For E = 70 GPa, the Euler buckling load (in kN, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: One end fixed, other end free → Le = 2L. Buckling occurs about the axis with the least I.
Exam tip: The deflected shape of a column fixed at the base and free at the top is one quarter of a sine wave; its mirror image completes the half wave of a pinned column of length 2L (figure).

questions.text: A long steel column with both ends pinned has a slenderness ratio of 120. For E = 210 GPa, the Euler critical (crippling) stress is nearly
solution: Concept: σcr = Pcr/A = π²EI/(ALe²) = π²E/(Le/k)², since I = Ak².
This is below the usual proportional limit of structural steel (about 200 to 250 MPa), so Euler's formula is valid here.
Exam tip: 45.8 MPa uses π instead of π². Critical stress depends only on E and slenderness, not on the absolute size.

questions.text: A solid cast-iron column of 100 mm diameter and 3 m length has both ends pinned. Using Rankine's formula with crushing stress σ<sub>c</sub> = 550 MPa and Rankine constant a = 1/1600, the crippling load (in kN) is ______
solution: Concept: Rankine: P = σcA / [1 + a(Le/k)²]. It blends crushing (short columns) and buckling (long columns).
Exam tip: For a solid circle k = d/4; for a rectangle kmin = b/√12. The crushing load alone (4320 kN) is ten times higher.

questions.text: For the same cross-sectional area, material and length, which section gives a column the highest Euler buckling load?
opts: a solid rectangle with depth twice the width
solution: Concept: Pcr = π²EAkmin²/Le². With A fixed, the section with the largest least radius of gyration wins.
Pushing material away from the centroid raises I = Ak² without adding area. A tube does this equally about every axis, so it has no weak axis.
Rectangles buckle about their weak axis; a solid circle or square keeps material near the centroid.
Answer: (D) the hollow circular tube.
Exam tip: This is why scaffold poles and many struts are tubes. Very thin walls can, however, fail by local buckling.

questions.text: A solid steel shaft of 50 mm diameter and 1.2 m length transmits a torque of 1.5 kN·m. For G = 80 GPa, the strain energy stored in the shaft (in J, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Torsional strain energy U = T²L/(2GJ) (area under the linear T–θ graph).
Exam tip: Equivalent form: U = (τmax²/4G) × volume for a solid shaft. Keep units in N and mm, then divide by 1000 for J.

questions.text: An axial load of 30 kN is applied suddenly (no drop height) to a steel bar of cross-sectional area 600 mm² and length 1.5 m. For E = 200 GPa, the maximum stress and the maximum elongation are
solution: Concept: For a suddenly applied load, work done P·δ equals strain energy σ²AL/(2E), which gives σ = 2P/A (twice the static value).
Exam tip: 50 MPa and 0.375 mm are the gradual-load values. A sudden load doubles both stress and elongation.

questions.text: A 500 N weight is dropped from a height of 20 mm onto the mid-span of the simply supported beam shown (span 2 m, EI = 200 kN·m²). Neglecting the beam's mass and any loss of energy, the maximum deflection at mid-span (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Energy balance W(h + δ) = ½kδ², with beam stiffness k = W/δst. This gives δ = δst[1 + √(1 + 2h/δst)].
δmax = 10.85 × 0.4167 = 4.52 mm (equivalent static load about 5.42 kN)
Exam tip: The same impact-factor formula works for bars, beams and springs. Only the static deflection changes.

questions.text: A cantilever of length L and flexural rigidity EI carries a uniformly distributed load w over its whole length. The strain energy stored due to bending is
solution: Concept: U = ∫ M²/(2EI) dx over the length.
From the loaded tip, M = wx²/2, so M² = w²x⁴/4
U = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>L</sup> w²x⁴/(8EI) dx = w²L⁵/(40EI)
Answer: (C) w²L⁵/(40EI).
Exam tip: Compare an end point load P: M = Px gives U = P²L³/(6EI). Integrate M² over the length; do not just multiply the end moment by the length.

questions.text: The stepped cantilever ABC shown is fixed at A. Portion AB (1 m) has flexural rigidity 2EI and portion BC (1 m) has EI, with EI = 600 kN·m². Using Castigliano's theorem, the deflection of the end C under the 5 kN load (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: δC = ∂U/∂P = ∫ M(∂M/∂P) dx/EI, taken segment by segment with each segment's own rigidity.
Measure x from C: M = Px, ∂M/∂P = x.
BC (0 to 1 m, EI): ∫ Px² dx/EI = P/(3EI)
AB (1 to 2 m, 2EI): ∫ Px² dx/(2EI) = P(8 − 1)/(6EI) = 7P/(6EI)
Exam tip: A uniform cantilever with EI throughout would give P(2)³/(3EI) = 22.2 mm. Stiffening the root section matters most because M is largest there.

questions.text: A propped cantilever of span L (fixed at A, propped at B at the same level) carries a UDL w over the whole span. Using the theorem of least work (Castigliano), the reaction at the prop B is
solution: Concept: Treat the prop reaction R as redundant. Since the prop does not move, ∂U/∂R = 0.
From B: M = Rx − wx²/2, ∂M/∂R = x
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>L</sup> (Rx − wx²/2)x dx = 0 → RL³/3 − wL⁴/8 = 0
R = 3wL/8; then RA = 5wL/8 and MA = wL²/8 (FBD below).
Exam tip: 5wL/8 is the fixed-end reaction, a common swap. 5P/16 is the prop reaction for a central point load.

questions.text: In the wall bracket shown, the inclined bar AC and the horizontal bar BC are pin-jointed at C and pinned to the wall at A and B (A is 1.2 m above B; BC = 1.6 m). Both bars have cross-sectional area 400 mm² and E = 200 GPa. Using Castigliano's theorem, the vertical deflection of C under the 30 kN load (in mm, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: For a pin-jointed frame, δ = Σ F(∂F/∂P)L/(AE) = Σ F²L/(PAE) when every F is proportional to P.
AC = √(1.6² + 1.2²) = 2.0 m. Joint C: FAC × 1.2/2.0 = 30 → FAC = 50 kN (tension); FBC = 50 × 1.6/2.0 = 40 kN (compression)
Exam tip: Signs do not matter in F²L terms, but they do when you use a unit load in a different direction from the real load.

questions.text: A 45° rectangular rosette reads ε<sub>0</sub> = 300 × 10⁻⁶, ε<sub>45</sub> = 650 × 10⁻⁶ and ε<sub>90</sub> = 500 × 10⁻⁶ (angles from the x-axis). The principal strains are
solution: Concept: For a 0°–45°–90° rosette: εx = ε0, εy = ε90, γxy = 2ε45 − ε0 − ε90.
ε1,2 = 400 ± 269.3 = 669.3 × 10⁻⁶ and 130.7 × 10⁻⁶; tan 2θp = 500/(−200) gives ε1 at 55.9° from the x-axis.
Exam tip: Gauges measure normal strain only. Shear strain always comes from the combination of the three readings, never from the 45° gauge alone.

questions.text: A 60° delta rosette (figure) on an aluminium plate reads ε<sub>a</sub> = 800 × 10⁻⁶, ε<sub>b</sub> = 200 × 10⁻⁶ and ε<sub>c</sub> = 500 × 10⁻⁶. For E = 70 GPa and ν = 0.33, the major principal stress (in MPa, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: For a 0°–60°–120° rosette: centre = (εa + εb + εc)/3 and radius = √[(εa − centre)² + ((εb − εc)/√3)²].
Exam tip: σ1 ≠ Eε1 (that gives 59.2 MPa). The Poisson coupling with ε2 must be included.

questions.text: A single strain gauge is bonded on the surface of a shaft in pure torsion, at 45° to the shaft axis. It reads 400 × 10⁻⁶. For G = 80 GPa, the maximum shear stress at the surface is
solution: Concept: Pure shear: the principal directions are at 45° to the axis, and ε45 = γ/2 (the principal strain).
Exam tip: 32 MPa forgets that ε45 is only half of γ. A gauge along the shaft axis would read zero in pure torsion.
